newsitem.title: USA: Sun Micro to buy Encore's storage business.
newsitem.headline: Sun Micro to buy Encore's storage business.

text.p: Sun Microsystems Inc said Thursday it agreed to buy the assets of Encore Computer Corp's storage business at a purchase price of $185 million for incorporation into its own storage products.
The company said the agreeemnt was subject to various closing conditions, including approval by Encore stockholders and regulatory approvals.

"Sun plans to integrate Encore's technology with our industry-leading Fibre Channel products to deliver on Sun's highly anticipated Open Storage Network architecture," said Kathleen Holmgren, vice president and general manager of Sun Microsystems' storage business unit.
As part of the deal, Sun will acquire Encore's DataShare software, which it said was the industry's only true mainframe/open systems data-sharing product.

Sun said the product provides a single, integrated view of corporate information, whether it is generated by a mainframe, open system or network server, eliminating the need for bulk file transfers between storage environments.

In January, Sun launched its assault on the high-end data center market with the introduction of its "Starfire" Ultra Enterprise 10000 machine and its RSM Array 2000 storage array. The acquisition enables it to integrate with a broader range of computer systems used in organization's data centers.
